item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
244
ABNT20 KNHC 280530
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fay, located well to the southwest of the Azores.

Central Subtropical Atlantic (AL91):
A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles
east-northeast of Bermuda is moving quickly east-northeastward. This
system is producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms, and it
could become a tropical depression over the next couple of days as
it turns eastward to east-southeastward and slows down over the
central Atlantic. Environmental conditions are expected to become
unfavorable for further development later this week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Mahoney

item.title: Summary for Tropical Depression Fay (AT1/AL062026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...FAY PERSISTS IN THE CENTRAL ATLANTIC... As of 9:00 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 the center of Fay was located near 27.9, -44.1 with movement SSW at 7 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1012 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 35 mph.

item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 280846
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fay Advisory Number  33
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 2026
 
...FAY PERSISTS IN THE CENTRAL ATLANTIC...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM GMT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...27.9N 44.1W
ABOUT 1210 MI...1945 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SSW OR 210 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1012 MB...29.89 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM GMT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 27.9 North, longitude 44.1 West. The
depression is moving toward the south-southwest near 7 mph (11 
km/h). A turn to the southwest and then to the west-southwest, 
along with an increase in forward motion, is expected over the next 
48 hours. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast during the next 48 hours.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1012 mb (29.89 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen/Mahoney

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 33
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 280848
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  33
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 2026

Fay's convection has persisted a bit longer overnight than 
previously seen the last couple of days. Dvorak intensity estimates 
appear to have picked up on this, with TAFB providing a subjective 
estimate of T2.0/30 kt. Based primarily on Fay's satellite 
presentation since the last advisory, the initial intensity was 
raised slightly to 30 kt, but Fay remains a tropical depression.

The forecast increase in forward speed, as well as a turn to the 
southwest, is becoming more evident on satellite imagery. For this 
advisory, the initial motion is set at 210/6 kt. Track guidance 
remains in fairly good agreement on Fay tracking to the southwest 
and then west-southwest as it is steered by the prevailing 
easterlies along the southern periphery of the Atlantic subtropical 
high. The greatest uncertainty across the guidance is the forward 
speed of the depression. The latest track forecast shows a faster 
forward speed over the next 48 h, in close agreement with the HCCA 
guidance.

So long as organized deep convection persists and scatterometry 
data depicts a closed low, Fay will remain a tropical depression. 
Even as SHIPS guidance shows Fay entering a favorable environment 
in terms of SSTs, vertical wind shear, and mid-level moisture, the 
current forecast thinking is that Fay's presence under mid- to 
upper-level ridging will drive convergence aloft and weaken its 
circulation to the point of dissipation. Global models agree on this 
and have Fay ultimately dissipating during the day Wednesday, with 
the exception of the UKMET, which holds onto the cyclone 
through the end of the week. The latest intensity forecast shows 
Fay becoming post-tropical late Tuesday, with dissipation a day or 
two later.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  28/0900Z 27.9N  44.1W   30 KT  35 MPH
 12H  28/1800Z 27.0N  44.8W   25 KT  30 MPH
 24H  29/0600Z 25.5N  46.3W   25 KT  30 MPH

 48H  30/0600Z 23.2N  49.3W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW

$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen/Mahoney
